coverage.assessment: The Civil Law/Common Law argument, the Pandects and Apthorp's proposal survive. The Gymnasium paragraph loses its motive ('ridded him') and its balancing tally ('foolish but... some purpose'), so the experiment reads only as failure.

The Sumner sighting jumps straight from running after the cab to encouragement, and no meeting is depicted. 'Beethoven might have this power' has lost its antecedent, the mechanical repetition. The London and Antwerp flash-forwards remain properly retrospective.
Sumner's cabman boast keeps its repeated 'I came to Berlin' with the 'or Rome' aside. The Apthorp/Adams Beethoven exchange keeps its speaker order and the others' laughter.

The ironic qualifiers in paragraph 1 survive ('when any one was looking at him'), and the boys are still twelve or thirteen. In the lecture paragraph, the self-deprecating 'not very quick' is gone, and so is the books-in-a-day comparison that substantiates 'worthless'.

The Marx line stays retrospective ('he had no idea'). The fifty-year London note and the half-century Antwerp note remain flashes forward. The young man's belief in Berlin is kept distinct from the later 'nightmare'.
The aphorisms and chiasmus survive. The Antwerp paragraph now ends flatly without the kneeling-at-the-Cross image, and the Beethoven awakening loses its astonishment and flower beats.

The dynamo metaphor stands, but its only illustrated effect is now bad ventilation. The mental 'polarizing' effect (morbid minds) and the 'viciously logical' irony are cut. The father's anti-Europe stance also loses the captious-critic counter-irony.
All four local endpoints are present, and all four partners still carry an echo. The Wagner partner sentence about New York was cut, but 'Gotterdammerung' and Brunhilde remain in 029.

strengths: All seven verbatim passages are preserved, including the full 'time wasted; studies neglected' catalogue and the closing cadence.
The paragraph 1 respectability catalogue keeps every ironic qualifier ('when any one was looking at him', 'towards a superior').
The Marx line and both fifty-year flash-forwards remain explicitly retrospective.
Sumner's boast keeps its repeated 'I came to Berlin' with the 'or Rome' self-correction.
The window-opening rebuke and the 'indictable nuisance' conclusion retain their escalating cadence.
summary: The revision keeps the chapter's skeleton, all seven verbatim passages, the continuity checks and all four dependencies. Its further cuts remove several small hinges and qualifiers: the Antwerp chronology and climax, the evidence for the lecture's worthlessness, the Sumner meeting, the Gymnasium's 'foolish but useful' tally, the morbid-minds effect of the State 'dynamo', and the Beethoven astonishment. The first draft had already removed the 'mechanical repetition' explanation that grounds 'this power'. None of these is a blocker, but together they thin the irony and the self-ledger.
